done_when: The forge.toml test command runs install, lint, typecheck, the API unit tests and the build, the full suites still run in GitHub's checks job, and a close on this laptop passes its tests

known.title: Required tests check fails because pnpm is no longer enabled

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - a pull request runs the required `tests` job. The previous step enabled Corepack when `pnpm` was absent; the new step calls `pnpm` directly after `actions/setup-node@v7`. [setup-node's documentation](https://github.com/actions/setup-node) says package managers must be pre-installed, and the [ubuntu-latest software inventory](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/ubuntu/Ubuntu2404-Readme.md) does not list pnpm. The step therefore fails with `pnpm: command not found` before installing or testing. This is new evidence about the generated GitHub job; the coordinator's no-guard instruction addressed the local `forge.toml` command.
findings.title: Required tests check fails because pnpm is no longer enabled

stop.reason: Owner chose the lighter local test command; one more round to restore enabling pnpm on GitHub's runner

why: Forge's local test run before a part is ready runs the whole website and browser suite, which times out on this laptop although GitHub passes it
